title: Developer Experience — Docs Standards, Quickstarts & API Examples (2026)
author: Asha Patel
content:
Overview

This document defines standards and operating procedures for Developer Experience (DevEx) documentation across SDK guides, quickstarts, API examples, docs-site operations, and our canonical support fixes. It contains:

- A short checklist and templates for SDK guides and quickstarts
- Standardized API example patterns (Python/Node/CLI)
- Docs-site publishing & rollback procedures
- Top support issues observed in 2025-2026 and canonical fixes
- Ownership, review cadence, and monitoring expectations

Audience

Primary: Developer Experience (DevEx) team, SDK owners, docs contributors, Solutions Engineering, and Support engineers.
Secondary: Product and Platform engineers who ship API changes that affect public docs.

Goals

1. Reduce time-to-first-success for new users (target: <10 minute quickstart run time).
2. Ensure examples are reliable, copy-pastable, and use production-safe defaults.
3. Provide clear operational runbooks for docs changes and incident-driven content updates.
4. Maintain a canonical mapping from common support issues -> reproducible checks & fixes.

1. SDK Guide & Quickstart Standards

1.1 Structure (required for every SDK guide)

- Title and short description (1-2 sentences).
- Quickstart (copy-paste runnable example): 6-12 lines for a minimal happy-path.
- Installation instructions (pip/npm/yarn) with exact package version.
- Auth / config section: describe environment variables and region config.
- Full example: realistic request (chat/generation/embeddings) with sample response.
- Error handling section: common errors with sample code and suggested remediation.
- Compatibility table: supported runtime versions (Python/Node), OS notes.
- Security notes: what data is sent, telemetry, and where logs appear.
- Links: related API reference, rate limits doc, and debugging runbook.

1.2 Quickstart Template (copy into new quickstarts)

- Title: <Feature> quickstart (e.g., Chat Quickstart — Python)
- TL;DR: 1-line summary + expected output
- Prereqs: account, API key, SDK version
- Install: copy-paste command
- Run: single command or 3-5 lines to run sample
- Validation: expected output and smoke checks
- Next steps & links

1.3 Example quickstart (Python — chat)

pip install redwood-inference==1.4.2

python - <<'PY'
from redwood import RedwoodClient
c = RedwoodClient(api_key="${REDWOOD_API_KEY}")
resp = c.chat.create(model="rwd-3b", messages=[{"role":"user","content":"Translate to Spanish: Hello world"}])
print(resp.choices[0].message.content)
PY

Notes: Quickstarts must use pinned SDK versions and avoid experimental flags. If a quickstart relies on Dedicated/Private-only features, mark it with label: "private-only".

2. API Examples and Patterns

2.1 Patterns to prefer

- Use the high-level client primitives (chat.create, embeddings.create) rather than raw HTTP unless demonstrating auth or curl usage.
- Prefer streaming examples for chat generation; show both blocking and streaming variants.
- Include examples for function/tool calling and structured output when applicable.

2.2 Minimal curl example (auth & region-aware)

curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-3b","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Summarize the release notes."}]}'

2.3 Node streaming example (canonical)

const { RedwoodClient } = require('redwood-inference');
const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });

(async () => {
  const stream = await client.chat.stream({ model: 'rwd-3b', messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'Write a haiku about latency.' }] });
  for await (const chunk of stream) {
    process.stdout.write(chunk.delta ?? '');
  }
})();

2.4 SDK versioning & compatibility

- Tag major SDK releases in repo and update examples when a breaking change is released.
- Patch releases may update examples if they fix reliability bugs; otherwise update the changelog but not the quickstarts.
- Quickstarts must pin to the latest minor release tested by DevEx (file: devex/quickstart-pinned-versions.md).

3. Docs Site Operating Procedures

3.1 Authoring & Review Workflow

- Draft in the staging space (devex-staging). Add reviewer(s) from relevant teams.
- Required reviewers: SDK owner + Support engineer for examples that touch shipping infra.
- Merge to production docs site after all reviewers sign off.
- Publish job should run link-check and run quickstart smoke tests.

3.2 Publishing checklist (pre-publish)

1. Run quickstart smoke tests (CI job: doc-quickstart-tests).
2. Verify sample API keys in tests are ephemeral and logged to secure store.
3. Confirm no TODOs or placeholder tokens remain.
4. Run link-check and copy-edit pass.
5. Assign labels and related_pages metadata.
6. Update release notes if change affects public API surface.

3.3 Rollback procedure

1. If a published change causes breakage, open an urgent docs rollback PR and tag @devex-oncall.
2. Revert the offending commit and redeploy the docs site.
3. Notify #devex and #support with a short summary and include affected quickstarts.
4. Create a follow-up to correct root cause and prevent recurrence.

3.4 Monitoring & Telemetry

- CI smoke test failures and broken quickstarts create PagerDuty alerts for devex-oncall.
- Track page views for quickstarts; target low-traffic quickstarts for consolidation every quarter.
- Support triage routes: if a doc receives >5 support tickets in a week, create a doc-action issue.

4. Top Support Issues & Canonical Fixes (2025-2026)

This section lists the most frequent problems customers report in Support and the canonical triage + fix steps.

Issue: 401 Unauthorized (most common)
- Symptom: API returns 401/403 for valid-looking requests.
- Checks:
  - Is REDWOOD_API_KEY set in the environment? (echo $REDWOOD_API_KEY)
  - Is the key for the correct environment (prod vs staging) or expired?
  - Is the request being routed to the correct region (e.g., us-west vs eu-west) — region-restricted keys will 401.
- Canonical fix:
  - Regenerate API key from Console -> API keys and update environment variable.
  - For region mismatch, use region-specific endpoint or correct the key scope.

Issue: Streaming stalls / partial responses
- Symptom: The client receives an initial chunk and then stalls indefinitely.
- Checks:
  - Confirm SDK client version supports streaming and server sent events (SSE) or websockets.
  - Network middleboxes or proxies blocking chunked transfer encoding.
  - Large initial system message or very long history triggers backpressure.
- Canonical fix:
  - Update SDK to latest patch (see pinned versions).
  - Add a keepalive or reconnect handler in streaming example (sample below).
  - Trim conversation history or use KV cache configuration for long sessions.

Sample reconnect pattern (Node)

async function streamWithReconnect(params) {
  let attempts = 0;
  while (attempts < 3) {
    try {
      const s = await client.chat.stream(params);
      for await (const chunk of s) process.stdout.write(chunk.delta ?? '');
      return;
    } catch (err) {
      attempts += 1;
      console.warn('stream error, retry', attempts, err.message);
      await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 500 * attempts));
    }
  }
  throw new Error('stream failed after retries');
}

Issue: High latency for embeddings or batching regressions
- Symptom: Embedding requests exceed the SLO (<200ms p50 for small batches).
- Checks:
  - Are requests being batched on the client? Check SDK batching config.
  - Is the model pinned to an overloaded instance type (review routing policy)?
  - Any recent config changes to continuous batching or prefix cache expiry.
- Canonical fix:
  - Adjust client batching parameters to reduce excessive micro-batching.
  - Move to recommended embeddings model variant for low-latency workloads.
  - Notify infra to check capacity if spike is observed.

Issue: Token billing mismatch (unexpectedly high costs)
- Symptom: Customer sees unexpectedly high token usage.
- Checks:
  - Are you using streaming? Check whether you are echoing prompts back into the model.
  - Are you using logprobs or debug flags that increase token reporting?
  - Is the model variant larger than intended (rwd-13b vs rwd-3b)?
- Canonical fix:
  - Confirm model parameter in request and advise smaller model variant if appropriate.
  - Audit prompt design for verbose instructions and remove unnecessary context.

Issue: Model hallucination / quality regression
- Symptom: Generated content contains factual errors or regression vs baseline.
- Checks:
  - Re-run the prompt on the pinned evaluation suite.
  - Check if the rollout included a new model or quantization profile.
- Canonical fix:
  - Roll back to previous model variant, open regression evaluation with Applied ML team.
  - Add guardrails (prompt templates, rerankers) and document in quickstart.

5. Ownership & Review Cadence

- Owner: DevEx content owner (Primary: Asha Patel) — responsible for doc health and quickstart smoke tests.
- SDK owners: responsible for SDK reference pages and sample code correctness.
- Support owner: triage and maintain canonical fixes list.
- Review cadence:
  - Major docs/quickstarts: review annually.
  - Quickstart smoke tests: run on every merge; failing tests trigger author notification.
  - Canonical fixes list: update quarterly or on major support pattern shifts.

6. Templates & File Naming Conventions

- File name format: short, hyphenated, year-suffixed (e.g., chat-quickstart-python-2026.json).
- Metadata must include title, space, author, owner_team, status, created_at, last_updated.
- Use labels to mark special cases: private-only, dedicated-only, deprecated.

Appendix A — Example metadata header (copyable)

{
  "title": "Chat quickstart — Python",
  "space": "eng-developer-experience",
  "author": "Asha Patel",
  "owner_team": "engineering",
  "status": "published",
  "created_at": "2026-01-10",
  "last_updated": "2026-01-10",
  "labels": ["quickstart","python","chat"]
}

Appendix B — Escalation contacts

- devex-oncall (PagerDuty)
- #devex (Slack)
- #support (Slack)
